_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 00:56:08Z)**_

It copies the file `.github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml` as it was in commit `cce7d6bcd` into your working folder.

- **`git show cce7d6bcd:.github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml`** prints that file's contents exactly as they were saved in that commit. It doesn't change your branch, the staging area or any other file. Your earlier command stops there; the next part is what writes the file.
- **`> .github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml`** writes that output to the same path on disk. If a file is already there, it gets overwritten.

The result is one new, untracked file. Nothing is staged or committed until you run `git add` and `git commit` yourself.

From the checks I ran before you stopped me:
- That commit is "[AI] Add temporary workflow to regenerate VRT snapshots", so the file is a GitHub Actions workflow for regenerating VRT screenshots.
- No file exists at that path yet, so nothing would be overwritten.
- I haven't read the file, so I don't know what triggers it. Once you commit and push it, GitHub could run it in CI, depending on its triggers.

In PowerShell 5.1, `>` doesn't copy the raw bytes. It re-encodes the text, usually adding a BOM (a hidden marker at the start of the file) and changing line endings. So the restored file might not match the original byte for byte, though GitHub Actions probably still reads it fine. Running it as `cmd /c "git show ... > ..."` or with `git restore --source=cce7d6bcd -- .github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml` gives an exact copy. `git restore` also overwrites any existing file at that path.

I can show you the workflow's contents before you decide whether to restore it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 01:00:30Z)**_

The VRT screenshots are PNG files in [packages/desktop-client/e2e/](packages/desktop-client/e2e/), in one folder per test file named `<test file>-snapshots/`. For example, the reports screenshots are in [reports.test.ts-snapshots/](packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts-snapshots/), with names like `Reports-loads-net-worth-graph-and-checks-visuals-1-chromium-linux.png`. Each test saves three screenshots, numbered `-1` to `-3`, one per theme.

The workflow doesn't list screenshots directly. It lists test files in `VRT_FILES` ([temp-update-vrt.yml:19-26](.github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml#L19-L26)), regenerates every screenshot those tests take, and commits the ones that changed. Right now it covers budget, command-bar, help-menu, rules, schedules, settings and transactions.

For your net worth change, the screenshots that matter are in [reports.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts):
- `loads net worth and cash flow reports` (line 33): the reports page with the Net Worth widget
- `loads net worth graph and checks visuals` (line 57): the full Net Worth report
- `opens the date range picker and checks visuals` (line 67): this one opens on the Net Worth page

To include them, add one line to `VRT_FILES`:

```yaml
    e2e/reports.test.ts
```

The workflow only runs when you push to the `fix/update-vrt-snapshots` branch (lines 7-9). To regenerate screenshots for your current branch, `feat/issue-11-net-worth-percentage`, you'd also need to add that branch to the trigger.

If you want, I can make both edits.

The quickest way is to create the demo again. When the app creates the demo or test budget, it first deletes any existing copy, then builds a fresh one ([app.ts:413-424](packages/loot-core/src/server/budgetfiles/app.ts#L413-L424)). With `yarn start`, that data lives in the browser's storage for `localhost:3001`, not in the repo, so nothing in git needs resetting.

**Option 1: create a new test file (in the app)**
1. Open your budget's menu (click the budget name at the top left) and choose **Close file**.
2. On the file list, click **Create test file**. That button appears only in development builds ([BudgetFileSelection.tsx:706-717](packages/desktop-client/src/components/manager/BudgetFileSelection.tsx#L706-L717)).

This replaces "Test Budget" with a freshly generated copy. It's built the same way as "Demo Budget", but it's a separate file, so your old Demo Budget stays in the list. Delete that one from the file list if you no longer want it.

**Option 2: wipe everything and start over**
1. With the app open at `http://localhost:3001`, open DevTools (F12), then go to **Application → Storage → Clear site data**.
2. Reload the page, choose **Don't use a server**, then **View demo**.

This removes every local budget and setting for that site, then recreates "Demo Budget" exactly as it was set up the first time.

The demo data is regenerated each time rather than restored from a saved copy, so it may not match your first demo transaction for transaction. In particular, the dates may be generated around today's date. It will have the same structure: the same kinds of accounts, categories and sample transactions.

# Running VRTs (Visual Regression Tests) in actualbudget/actual

VRTs are ordinary Playwright e2e tests in `packages/desktop-client/e2e/*.test.ts` that call:

```ts
await expect(target).toMatchThemeScreenshots();
```

`toMatchThemeScreenshots()` is a custom matcher defined in
`packages/desktop-client/e2e/fixtures.ts`. `target` is a `Page` or a `Locator` —
**prefer a tight locator** (e.g. a popover or panel) over the whole page to
reduce noise from charts and data.

## Key mechanics

- **No-op without `VRT=true`.** In a plain e2e run the matcher passes
  immediately, so `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run playwright test <file> -g "<name>"`
  verifies the interaction flow cheaply without needing snapshots — always do
  this first.
- **With `VRT=true`, each call captures three themes** (`auto` i.e. light,
  `dark`, `midnight`), producing numbered snapshots:
  `<file>.test.ts-snapshots/<Describe>-<test-name>-N-chromium-linux.png`.
  One test with 2 assertions → 6 PNGs.
- **Masking:** elements with `data-vrt-mask="true"` are masked out of
  screenshots. Use it for volatile content (real dates, version numbers).
- **Diff tolerance is strict:** `maxDiffPixels: 5`, `threshold: 0.05`
  (`packages/desktop-client/playwright.config.ts`).
- **Snapshots are Linux-only.** Committed snapshots end in
  `-chromium-linux.png` and must be generated inside the Playwright docker
  image. A host run on macOS writes `-chromium-darwin.png`, which CI ignores.

## Writing a new VRT

Import from the local fixtures, not `@playwright/test`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from './fixtures';
```

Patterns to copy:

- Date-picker popover VRT: `e2e/transactions.test.ts` ("by date").
- Report VRTs: `e2e/reports.test.ts`.
- Tests use the demo budget (`ConfigurationPage.createTestFile()`), whose data
  is pinned (date ranges show 2016), so snapshots are largely date-stable.
- Popovers render with a `[data-popover]` attribute — a good screenshot
  locator.
- Page models live in `e2e/page-models/`.

## Generating snapshots locally (docker)

Run all yarn commands from the repo root.

1. Start the dev server with HTTPS (background it; ready when
   `https://localhost:3001` returns 200 — `ignoreHTTPSErrors` is already set in
   the Playwright config):

   ```sh
   HTTPS=true yarn start
   ```

2. The container runs with `--network host`. On Linux it can reach
   `https://localhost:3001` directly. On macOS/Windows it cannot — get the
   machine's LAN IP (`ipconfig getifaddr en0` on macOS) and use
   `https://<LAN_IP>:3001` instead.

3. Run the Playwright docker image directly. The `bin/run-vrt` wrapper passes
   `-it`, which fails without a TTY, so in an agent shell invoke docker
   yourself:

   ```sh
   docker run --rm --network host -v "$(pwd)":/work/ -w /work/ \
     mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-jammy /bin/bash -c \
     "E2E_START_URL=https://<HOST>:3001 yarn vrt --update-snapshots -g '<test name>' <file>.test.ts"
   ```

   Pin the image tag to the repo's Playwright version (`@playwright/test` in
   `packages/desktop-client/package.json` — currently 1.61.1 →
   `v1.61.1-jammy`). The equivalent user-facing wrapper is
   `yarn vrt:docker --e2e-start-url https://<HOST>:3001 --update-snapshots`.

4. **Always scope `--update-snapshots`** with `-g`/file args to the new or
   changed test only — an unscoped update rewrites every screenshot in the
   repo.

5. Verify by re-running the exact same command **without**
   `--update-snapshots`; it must pass.

6. Optionally Read one generated PNG to sanity-check it shows the intended UI,
   then commit the test + PNGs (commit messages need the `[AI]` prefix — see
   the committing-actual-changes skill).

## Fallback without docker

Commit only the test file; CI generates the snapshots when someone comments
`/update-vrt` on the PR (`.github/workflows/vrt-update-generate.yml`).

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

Those jobs skip on purpose. Each one is set to run only in the official `actualbudget/actual` repo, and your PR is in your class fork, `CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget`. The workflow files you inherited from upstream contain this condition:

```yaml
if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'
```

In a fork that condition is false, so GitHub marks the job as skipped rather than failed. None of the skips are caused by your code. All 31 checks that did run on PR #124 passed, including lint, typecheck, test, knip and the visual regression tests.

| Skipped job | Workflow | Why it skips |
|---|---|---|
| `autofix` | [autofix.yml:16](.github/workflows/autofix.yml#L16) | Upstream repo only |
| `mobile` | [build.yml:117](.github/workflows/build.yml#L117) | Upstream repo only; it also needs paid macOS build machines from Depot, a CI service |
| `check-release-notes` | [release-notes.yml:17-19](.github/workflows/release-notes.yml#L17-L19) | Upstream repo only, and only on pull requests |
| `generate-release-notes` | [release-notes.yml:72](.github/workflows/release-notes.yml#L72) | Upstream repo only, and only on pushes (when releasing) |
| `Report E2E results to Depot` | [e2e-test.yml:114](.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml#L114) | Upstream repo only, and only in the merge queue (`merge_group`) |

Most of these use the upstream project's Depot account or its release credentials, which a fork doesn't have. So they're turned off outside the main repo.

The one you might miss is `check-release-notes`. It's what checks your release note file in `upcoming-release-notes/` against the format rules, so in your fork nobody checks it automatically.

266	function alignInternalTransferDates(
267	  data: AccountBalanceData[],
268	  transferLegs: TransferLeg[],
269	  range: IntervalRange,
270	) {
271	  const accountsById = new Map(data.map(account => [account.id, account]));
272	  const transfersById = new Map(transferLegs.map(leg => [leg.id, leg]));
273	  const processed = new Set<string>();

275	  transferLegs.forEach(leg => {
276	    if (processed.has(leg.id)) {
277	      return;
278	    }
279	
280	    const counterpart = transfersById.get(leg.transfer_id);
281	    if (
282	      !counterpart ||
283	      counterpart.transfer_id !== leg.id ||
284	      counterpart.account === leg.account ||
285	      counterpart.amount + leg.amount !== 0 ||
286	      !accountsById.has(leg.account) ||
287	      !accountsById.has(counterpart.account)
288	    ) {
289	      return;
290	    }
291	
292	    processed.add(leg.id);
293	    processed.add(counterpart.id);
294	
295	    if (leg.date === counterpart.date) {
296	      return;
297	    }
298	
299	    const [earlier, later] =
300	      leg.date < counterpart.date ? [leg, counterpart] : [counterpart, leg];
301	
302	    const account = accountsById.get(earlier.account);
303	    if (account) {
304	      moveTransferLeg(account, earlier, later.date, range);
305	    }
306	  });
307	}

309	function moveTransferLeg(
310	  account: AccountBalanceData,
311	  leg: TransferLeg,
312	  laterDate: string,
313	  range: IntervalRange,
314	) {
315	  const { startDate, endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx } = range;
316	  if (laterDate < startDate) {

318	  }
319	
320	  if (leg.date < startDate) {

322	  } else {
323	    if (leg.date > endDate) {

326	    const originalKey = getIntervalKey(leg.date, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx);
327	    const originalBalance = account.balances[originalKey];
328	    if (!originalBalance) {

332	  }
333	
334	  if (laterDate > endDate) {

336	  }

338	  const intervalKey = getIntervalKey(laterDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx);
339	  const balance = account.balances[intervalKey];
340	  if (balance) {
341	    balance.amount += leg.amount;
342	  } else {
343	    account.balances[intervalKey] = { date: intervalKey, amount: leg.amount };
344	  }
345	}

347	function getIntervalKey(

349	  interval: string,
350	  firstDayOfWeekIdx: string,
351	) {

354	  }
355	  if (interval === 'Weekly') {

357	  }
358	  if (interval === 'Yearly') {
359	    return date.slice(0, 4);
360	  }
361	  return monthUtils.getMonth(date);
362	}

364	function recalculate(

366	  startDate: string,
367	  endDate: string,
368	  locale: Locale,
369	  interval: string = 'Monthly',

414	      networth: number;

416	    }>
417	  >((arr, intervalItem, idx) => {
418	    let debt = 0;
419	    let assets = 0;
420	    let total = 0;
421	    const last = arr.length === 0 ? null : arr[arr.length - 1];
422	
423	    const balances: Record<string, number> = {};

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 20:25:35Z)**_

I added `totalChangePercent` next to `totalChange` in the net worth report's data ([net-worth-spreadsheet.ts:494-524](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/net-worth-spreadsheet.ts#L494-L524)). It's stored as a plain percentage, so 12.5 means 12.5%, and nothing displays it yet. Formatting and lint pass on the file; I haven't run the type check or tests.

How it's calculated:
- **No change:** it's stored as `0`.
- **Normal case:** it's the change divided by the absolute value of the starting net worth, times 100. Because the bottom of the fraction is always positive, a drop in net worth always gives a negative percentage and a rise always gives a positive one. That still holds when net worth started below zero: going from -1,000 to -1,500 gives -50%.
- **Net worth started at exactly 0 and then changed:** it's stored as `null`. Your "no change" rule doesn't cover this case, and there's no meaningful percentage to divide out, so I used `null` to avoid a division by zero. When you build the display, you can show something like "—" for it.

**Not strictly year-to-date:** `totalChange` measures the change across whatever date range the report is set to, so the new percentage does too. It only matches year-to-date when the report's range starts in January.

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

97	function slugify(input: string): string {

106	// makes an attempt to find an existing open PR from <username>:<branch>
107	async function getActivePr(
108	  username: string,
109	): Promise<{ number: number; title: string } | undefined> {
110	  if (!username) {

113	  const branchName = await execAsync('git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD');
114	  if (!branchName) {

118	  return getPrNumberFromHead(forkHead);

123	): Promise<{ number: number; title: string } | undefined> {
124	  try {
125	    // head is a weird query parameter in this API call. If nothing matches, it
126	    // will return as if the head query parameter doesn't exist. To get around
127	    // this, we make the page size 2 and only return the number if the length.
128	    const resp = await fetch(
129	      'https://api.github.com/repos/actualbudget/actual/pulls?state=open&per_page=2&head=' +
130	        head,
131	    );
132	    if (!resp.ok) {
133	      console.warn('error fetching from github pulls api:', resp.status);
134	      return undefined;
135	    }
136	    const ghResponse = await resp.json();
137	    if (ghResponse?.length === 1) {
138	      return ghResponse[0];
139	    } else {
140	      return undefined;
141	    }
142	  } catch (e) {
143	    console.warn('error fetching from github pulls api:', e);
144	  }
145	}
146	
147	function getFileContents(type: string, username: string, summary: string) {
148	  return `---
149	category: ${type}
150	authors: [${username}]
151	---
152	
153	${summary}
154	`;
155	}
156	
157	// simple exec that fails silently and returns an empty string on failure
158	async function execAsync(cmd: string, errorLog?: string): Promise<string> {
159	  return new Promise<string>(res => {
160	    exec(cmd, (error, stdout) => {
161	      if (error) {
162	        console.log(errorLog);
163	        res('');
164	      } else {
165	        res(stdout.trim());
166	      }
167	    });
168	  });
169	}

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 21:27:21Z)**_

Run these from the repo root:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `yarn lint` | Checks formatting and lint rules without changing any files. |
| `yarn lint:fix` | Same checks, but fixes whatever it can automatically. |
| `yarn test` | Runs the unit tests across all packages. Results are cached, so unchanged packages are skipped. |
| `yarn typecheck` | Checks TypeScript types. |

Before opening a PR, `yarn lint`, `yarn typecheck` and `yarn test` together cover what the automated checks on GitHub run. For this branch, I've only run lint and formatting on the files we changed, plus the type check, and all of those passed. I haven't run the full `yarn lint` or `yarn test`.

60	async function runReport({
61	  accounts,
62	  accountQueryResults,
63	  linkedTransfers = [],
64	  start = '2026-07',
65	  end = '2026-08',
66	  interval = 'Monthly',
67	  earliestTransactionDate = '2026-07-01',
68	}: {
69	  accounts: AccountEntity[];
70	  accountQueryResults: AccountQueryResult[];
71	  linkedTransfers?: LinkedTransfer[];
72	  start?: string;
73	  end?: string;
74	  interval?: string;
75	  earliestTransactionDate?: string;
76	}) {
77	  const remainingAccountResults = [...accountQueryResults];
78	
79	  initServer({
80	    'make-filters-from-conditions': async () => ({ filters: [] }),
81	    'get-earliest-transaction': async () => ({
82	      date: earliestTransactionDate,
83	    }),
84	    query: async query => {
85	      if (query.selectExpressions.includes('transfer_id')) {
86	        const transferFilter = query.filterExpressions.find(
87	          expression => 'transfer_id' in expression,
88	        );
89	        const accountIds = getOneOfValues(transferFilter?.account);
90	        const transactionIds = getOneOfValues(transferFilter?.id);
91	        const endDate = getUpperBound(transferFilter?.date);
92	
93	        return {
94	          data: linkedTransfers.filter(
95	            leg =>
96	              (accountIds.length === 0 || accountIds.includes(leg.account)) &&
97	              (transactionIds.length === 0 ||
98	                transactionIds.includes(leg.id)) &&
99	              (!endDate || leg.date <= endDate),
100	          ),
101	          dependencies: [],
102	        };
103	      }
104	
105	      const data = remainingAccountResults.shift();
106	      if (data === undefined) {
107	        throw new Error('Unexpected account query');
108	      }
109	      return { data, dependencies: [] };
110	    },
111	  });
112	
113	  let report: SpreadsheetData | undefined;
114	  const spreadsheet = createSpreadsheet(
115	    start,
116	    end,
117	    accounts,
118	    [],
119	    'and',
120	    enUS,
121	    interval,
122	    '0',
123	  );
124	
125	  // The net worth factory does not use its spreadsheet dependency.
126	  await spreadsheet(undefined as never, data => {
127	    report = data;
128	  });
129	
130	  if (!report) {
131	    throw new Error('Spreadsheet did not produce report data');
132	  }
133	  return report;
134	}
135	
136	function getOneOfValues(value: unknown) {
137	  if (
138	    typeof value === 'object' &&
139	    value !== null &&
140	    '$oneof' in value &&
141	    Array.isArray(value.$oneof)
142	  ) {
143	    return value.$oneof.filter(item => typeof item === 'string');
144	  }
145	  return [];
146	}
147	
148	function getUpperBound(value: unknown) {
149	  if (
150	    typeof value === 'object' &&
151	    value !== null &&
152	    '$lte' in value &&
153	    typeof value.$lte === 'string'
154	  ) {
155	    return value.$lte;
156	  }
157	  return null;
158	}
159	
160	afterEach(async () => {
161	  await clearServer();
162	});

|---|---|

| -$1,000 improves by $500 | +50% |

The two negative-start rows confirm a decrease always comes out negative, even when net worth started below zero.

**Display tests** in [Change.test.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/Change.test.tsx) check what's shown on screen:

- 33.333…% is rounded to one decimal place, `(+33.3%)`.

- The `null` case shows as `(--)`.
